history.summary: The lowest absolute entry in the batch at $1.2M, with $1,359 psf sitting ~8% under the $1,483 URA median, in a large 928-unit 2016 development with good resale depth (228 txns). But it's served only by Kangkar LRT (no MRT), reviews flag space inefficiency, and connectivity is its structural ceiling — a value-led Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: Positives: cheapest entry here ($1.2M), $1,359 psf is ~8% below the $1,483 median, the development is large (928 units) and reasonably young (2016) with healthy 228-txn liquidity and 6.0% resale CAGR. The decisive negative is location: the only rail access is Kangkar LRT (710m), one stop on the Sengkang loop — there is no nearby MRT, which structurally caps tenant pool and resale appeal versus MRT-served D19 peers, and reviews note inefficient/wasteful layouts. Cheap and liquid, but the connectivity ceiling keeps it balanced rather than a buy.

history.summary: A 1,109 sqft 3BR in Upper Serangoon, asking $1,578 PSF — a ~6% premium to the $1,483 median — at a low $1.75M absolute. The 6.0% resale CAGR (228 txns), 928-unit liquidity and frontier position are positives, but connectivity is weak (only an LRT 710m away, MRT is far), units are noted as space-inefficient, and the above-median ask undercuts the value case, landing it at Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: Positives: $1.75M is the second-lowest quantum in the batch (deep buyer pool), 928 units give strong liquidity, on the efficient frontier, and a 6.0% URA resale CAGR over 228 transactions. But the offsets are real: asking $1,578 PSF is ~6% above the $1,483 median, so you are paying up; connectivity is genuinely poor — the nearest rail is Kangkar LRT 710m/9-min away and the true MRT is a further hop, a structural drag in transit-dependent D19; reviewers flag inefficient layouts/space wastage; and D19's broad new-supply pipeline (Sengkang/Punggol) competes for the same tenant/buyer base. Solid building, but priced above median with a connectivity handicap nets to Neutral.

history.summary: Mega 921-unit 99-LH (2016) project in Hougang/Upper Serangoon - by far the deepest data of the five (228 appreciation txns, 23 cohort txns). Asking $1,359 psf sits modestly below the project's recent avg (~$1,393 psf, 6mo ~$1,478) and the discount signals (-22.1% age_adj, -6.3% cohort) are real and well-supported rather than quirks. Liquid, ~3.8% yield, OCR with a dated CRL Punggol Extension (2032) catalyst. A solid value-and-liquidity Buy.
history.rating_rationale: This is the only contender with statistically robust signals: 228 appreciation txns and 23 cohort txns make the -22.1% age_adj_premium and -6.3% cohort discount trustworthy, not artifacts. Verified 12mo project avg ~$1,393 psf (6mo ~$1,478, range $1,038-$1,548); the $1,359 asking for a 2BR is modestly below market and below the 6mo run-rate. Per v3.4, verified cheap-vs-peers in an OCR district (D19, realized fwd ~+4%) is the strongest robust signal. The 921-unit scale gives genuine resale and rental liquidity that the boutiques lack, and the Cross Island Line Punggol Extension (target 2032) is a dated medium-term catalyst. Capped at medium confidence because the discount is modest (not deep) and it is a 99-LH facing lease decay.
red_flags: 99-year leasehold from 2016 - lease decay is a long-run drag, though 2016 vintage is still young
Mega-project (921 units) means continuous internal resale supply that can cap PSF upside
Hougang/Upper Serangoon is further from the nearest MRT than the city-fringe peers (connectivity is bus-reliant until CRL)
catalysts: Cross Island Line - Punggol Extension (target 2032) improving Hougang/north-east connectivity (dated medium-term catalyst)
Reservoir-adjacent, extensive facilities, family-friendly - strong owner-occupier and rental demand
Deep liquidity (921 units) supports a clean 5-7yr exit
~3.8% gross yield with 2BR units reaching ~4.2% per market data

history.summary: A 1,065 sqft 3BR/2-bath at Riversails (D19, 920 units, 99-yr from Dec 2011, TOP 2016) asking $1,499,800 / $1,408 psf. Genuine 3BR (URA rental filings: 22 three-bedroom contracts in the 1,000-1,100 sqft bucket vs 2 two-bedroom), sound mega-project, deepest liquidity in its peer set. But the headline discount is most likely a low-floor artifact that cannot be verified: every one of the three floor-01-to-05 prints in this exact 1,065 sqft line is the low outlier of its year (-9% to -15%), and $1,408 psf lands at the top of the low-floor mark-to-market band. Carry is thin (3.2% gross on URA-exact rent) and rent has been flat since 2023 while band psf rose 15%. Fair-to-cheap under either reading, edge unproven under one of them.
history.rating_rationale:
The MMR's 813 rests on a value signal I can only half-confirm. Against the project's own comps the ask looks better than the -6.4% vs project median suggests: Riversails' 3BR band (1,000-1,160 sqft) is the one band trading ABOVE the project median, at a $1,610 psf 2026 median (n=4), so $1,408 is -12.5% vs its true comp set, and -9.2% vs age-adjusted D19 same-size peers. The same-size Feb-26 print was $1,655,000 ($1,553 psf, floor 06-10) - this ask is $155k below it.

That gap has a mundane explanation the data supports. The 1,065 sqft line has 13 prints since 2021, three on floors 01-05, and all three are their year's low: Dec-21 $1,051 vs Aug-21 $1,192 (-12%); Jul-23 $1,314 vs Mar-23 $1,450 (-9%); Jun-24 $1,267 vs May-24 $1,491 (-15%). Scale the Feb-26 mid-floor print by that and a low-floor 1,065 today marks at ~$1,320-1,400 psf = $1.41-1.49M. The ask is $1,408 psf / $1.4998M - at the TOP of that range, i.e. mark-to-market, not a discount. PropertyGuru served no floor_level for this listing and Riversails has no researched stack profile, so the single variable deciding whether this is a -9% bargain or a fairly-priced low-floor unit is unobserved. The v3.12 low-floor trust rules never fired for exactly that reason - no floor data, no unit number to match a stack. Note also the 1,033 sqft line shows almost NO floor penalty (May-26, floor 01-05, $1,597 psf), so this is a quirk of the 1,065 line specifically - which points at a position/facing problem in those stacks, not a generic floor effect.

Two research corrections to the fact sheet, both in the listing's favour or neutral. (1) momentum -0.921 is a size-mix artifact, not deceleration: the 2026 print sample skews to the 900-sqft band, while the 3BR 1,000-1,160 band went $1,154 (2021) -> $1,398 (2023) -> $1,524 (2025) -> $1,610 (2026 YTD), +6.9%/yr and still +5.6% YTD. I do not hold momentum against this unit. (2) 'nearest future MRT: Defu, 977m' is wrong - Defu (CRL, 2030) is ~3.3km away. Nearest heavy rail is Buangkok at ~1.19km (geocoded); Kangkar LRT is the 710m walk. The relevant future stations are Hougang CRL (~2.1km) and Riviera on the CRL Punggol Extension (~1.5km, 2032). Neither is walkable, and per current priors the future-infra channel has no measured forward power anyway - story, not signal.

Against it: carry is weak and unimproving. URA rental filings for this exact type (3BR, 1,000-1,100 sqft, 22 contracts) median $4,025; the 2025-26 filings run $3,850-$4,400 with the latest (Apr-26) at $4,050. The scorer's $4,200 is a touch generous. At $4,000 that is 3.2% gross / ~1.9% net, and rent has gone sideways since 2023 while the band's psf rose 15% - the price run is multiple expansion, not rent-supported. The run's 6.0%/yr all-cash ROI inherits the 6.04% trailing CAGR, which the backtest says has ~zero forward power; re-scored at the OCR baseline 4.2% with the URA-exact $4,000 rent, all-cash ROI is 4.3%/yr (5yr) / 4.4%/yr (7yr). That is the honest number.

Also: it is the cheapest 3BR ask in the project by ~$190k (live book: $1.69M, $1.75M, $1.88M, all the 1,108 line) and has sat at an unchanged $1,499,800 since first seen 7 Jun 2026, ~7 weeks. This repo's own lesson is that a persistent cheapest-in-project ask that has not cleared is more often a floor/facing defect than a bargain. Riversails reviews independently flag two things that would produce exactly this price: stacks facing Upper Serangoon Road are noisy, and the 3-bedders are cramped. Block 20's orientation is unresearched.

Net: not an Avoid - there is no format artifact here (real 3BR, standard enclosed area, 328 units of the same format, 228 resales in 5 years, 1,342 lifetime transactions per realsmart), the lease is a non-issue (86 years left, ~79 at exit), OCR is the favoured region, and under either floor reading the price is fair rather than rich. But not a Buy either: the entire edge over a market-typical OCR hold rests on a floor level nobody has disclosed, and the baseline-prior return is ~4.3%/yr all-cash on a 1.9% net carry. This flips to a Buy on one fact - confirm floor 08 or higher and a non-road-facing aspect and the -9% is real; confirm floors 01-05 or an Upper Serangoon Road aspect and it is mark-to-market and should be passed.
red_flags: Floor level unknown and it decides the call. The 1,065 sqft line's three floor-01-05 prints are each their year's low (-9%, -12%, -15% vs same-year mid-floor). Scaled to the Feb-26 mid-floor print ($1,553 psf), a low-floor 1,065 marks at $1,320-1,400 psf = $1.41-1.49M; the ask is $1,408 psf / $1.4998M, at the TOP of that band. PropertyGuru returned no floor_level; no stack profile exists for Riversails; the v3.12 low-floor trust rules could not fire.

Cheapest 3BR ask in the project by ~$190k, unchanged for ~7 weeks (first seen 7 Jun 2026 at $1,499,800). Live 3BR book is $1.69M / $1.75M / $1.88M. A persistent cheapest-in-project ask that has not cleared usually signals a defect, not value.

Thin and stagnant carry: URA filings for this exact type (3BR, 1,000-1,100 sqft, n=22) median $4,025/mo, 2025-26 range $3,850-$4,400, Apr-26 at $4,050. Rent flat since 2023 while the band's psf rose ~15% ($1,398 -> $1,610). 3.2% gross / ~1.9% net. The price run is multiple expansion, not rent-supported.

The run's 6.0%/yr all-cash ROI inherits the 6.04% trailing URA CAGR, which the backtest gives ~zero forward power. At the OCR baseline (4.2%) with the URA-exact $4,000 rent, all-cash ROI is 4.3%/yr (5yr) / 4.4%/yr (7yr).

No MRT. Kangkar LRT 710m walk; nearest heavy rail Buangkok ~1.19km geocoded. The record's 'nearest future MRT: Defu 977m' is a data error - Defu (CRL) is ~3.3km. Hougang CRL ~2.1km, Riviera (CRL Punggol Extension, 2032) ~1.5km. Neither walkable; future-infra has no measured forward power regardless.

Smallest 3BR line in the project (standard 3BR runs 1,033-1,108 sqft) on 2 baths, and Riversails reviews specifically call the 3-bedders 'a little too small for comfort'. At a 5-7yr exit it competes against the 1,108 line and the 1,367 sqft 4BR inside the same development.

Facing unresearched. Reviewers warn off stacks facing Upper Serangoon Road for traffic noise; the subject is Block 20 and its orientation is unknown. Combined with the unknown floor, two of the three variables that set price within this project are unobserved.

realsmart REALSCORE unavailable: realsmart.sg/p/riversails resolves and confirms the development (920 units, 1,342 transactions, $1.3B+, latest 17 Jun 2026, 99-yr from 7 Dec 2011, Benefit Investments / Allgreen) but serves the lite template with no REALSCORE, % profitable or annualized-return tiles, and the /map rung returned nothing this run. Fields left null rather than guessed.
catalysts: Deep, real liquidity - the strongest thing here. 920 units, 328 of them 3BR, 228 URA resales in 5 years (~46/yr), 1,342 lifetime transactions totalling $1.3B+ (realsmart /p page, latest 17 Jun 2026). Buyer-pool depth is one of the few levers that survives clustering in the backtest (std_beta +0.16).

The 3BR band is the project's best-performing band, and the algo's momentum reading is wrong about it. 1,000-1,160 sqft median psf: $1,154 (2021) -> $1,281 (2022) -> $1,398 (2023) -> $1,420 (2024) -> $1,524 (2025) -> $1,610 (2026 YTD) = +6.9%/yr, still +5.6% YTD. The -0.921 momentum is a size-mix artifact from a 900-sqft-heavy 2026 print sample.

Genuinely cheap versus the right comp set IF the floor holds up. The 3BR band trades ABOVE the project median ($1,610 vs $1,483), so the true gap is -12.5% vs 2026 band prints and -9.2% vs age-adjusted D19 same-size peers - not the -6.4% on the fact sheet. Same-size Feb-26 print: $1,655,000 ($1,553 psf, floor 06-10).

Bedroom count is real, not a relabel. URA rental filings show 22 three-bedroom contracts in the 1,000-1,100 sqft bucket against 2 two-bedroom; bed_bands verdict 'ok' (band 1,050-1,350, 70 contracts). This is the compact end of a genuine 3BR format, not a 2+study.
OCR region - the strongest measured forward-region prior (realized +3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%). Real, but generic to any OCR asset, not a Riversails edge.
Lease is a non-issue: 99 years from 7 Dec 2011 leaves 86 years, ~79 at a 7-year exit - far clear of CPF pro-rating or bank-LTV thresholds.
Quantum fits the mandate with room ($1.4998M against a $1.8M 3BR budget) and sits in the deepest OCR buyer band, where HDB upgrader demand is thickest.
Sound development fundamentals: Allgreen-built, 2016 TOP, 12 blocks of 18 storeys, three pool areas and two tennis courts, reviews describe it as well-maintained and quiet despite its size.

The important read is not the level but the trend: filings were $4,200-$4,500 back in 2023 and are $3,850-$4,050 now, i.e. rent has drifted DOWN while the band's psf rose ~15% over the same window. Riversails' rent ceiling is set by the LRT-only location and a large in-project supply of competing 3BRs (328 units of the format), and there is no evidence of it lifting. Count this as carry only - per current priors yield is never appreciation, and a project whose price gain is entirely multiple expansion has less cushion if OCR sentiment cools.

The momentum -0.921 should be disregarded - it is a 2026 size-mix artifact, and the subject's own band accelerated rather than stalled.

agent_evaluation.stack_notes:
No researched profile for Riversails - stack_profile status is 'not_researched', so nothing was joined. This is the binding gap. Address is Block 20 (Riversails is blocks 2-24 Upper Serangoon Crescent, 12 blocks x 18 storeys); orientation of Block 20 is unknown, and resident reviews specifically warn off stacks facing Upper Serangoon Road for traffic noise while the river/reservoir-facing aspects are the prized ones.

The floor evidence I could build from URA prints alone: within the 1,000-1,160 sqft band, mean psf relative to the band-year median runs 0.897 on floors 01-05 (n=9), 0.991 on 06-10 (n=28), 1.000 on 11-15 (n=16), 1.019 on 16-20 (n=14). But the penalty is concentrated in the 1,065 line, not the band: all three of that line's 01-05 prints are their year's low (-9% to -15%), whereas the 1,033 line's low-floor prints show almost none (May-26, floor 01-05, $1,597 psf against a $1,610 band median). That asymmetry suggests the low-floor 1,065 stacks specifically sit somewhere undesirable - road frontage, a driveway, or an overlooked aspect - rather than suffering a generic height discount.

Running /research-development on Riversails before any viewing would pay for itself here, and the one question to put to the agent is the unit number: floor 08+ on a non-Upper-Serangoon-Road aspect makes this a Buy; floors 01-05 or a road aspect makes it mark-to-market and a pass.
